newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro council must be open to "pre-ins"-Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Euro council must be open to "pre-ins"-Belgium.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Monday he supported the idea of an economic council to co-ordinate policies inside European monetary union, but this must not exclude countries waiting to join the new single currency.

He said a French proposal for such a "stability council", attacked by the Bundesbank as a potential threat to the independence of the future European Central Bank, had not been discussed at Monday's ECOFIN Council.
But asked about his own views of the French proposal, he said, "it seemed to me an idea which responded to a real need."
"No one is questioning that the fact of creating monetary union will create a need for improved co-ordination," he told a news conference.

He said his main concern was to ensure that such a council did not exclude countries waiting to join monetary union, whose economies were judged to be not quite ready according to Maastricht treaty criteria, the so-called "pre-ins".
"The pre-ins should take part in this body," he said.

He also said he was convinced that the European Union would need to define the difference between countries which were waiting to join the single currency after its launch in January 1999, and those unlikely, or unwilling, to join near-term.

He said European finance ministers had discussed informally who should represent the interests of the euro zone internationally -- a question raised by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel. It made no decisions on this.
French officials have suggested the stability council could have a rotating presidency, similar to the Group of Seven rich nations, to represent the euro zone in international talks.
Maystadt said the euro zone could also be represented by the European Commission, the Council and the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner to the European Central Bank (ECB).
